subcomponents.title: Uses scene-kit APIs without bypassing or duplicating them

criteria.rationale: Talk passes its steps to the kit's Presentation component. The shared Scene uses exported kit primitives for its diagram, while Presentation and Stage provide navigation and scene hosting.
evidence: Talk renders <Presentation steps={STEPS}>.
Scene renders SceneLayer, Box, Arrow, Label, Presence, and other kit exports; Stage renders the active Scene from each step.

subcomponents.title: Uses stable identities and appropriate grouped-scene architecture

criteria.rationale: The nine entries generated from beats use the same Scene and groupKey. Stage keeps one keyed canvas mounted across those adjacent steps. Separately, Scene passes presentation-owned entity IDs to kit nodes that use them as motion layoutId values; step cards receive stable IDs from stepCard(index).
evidence: STEPS maps every beat to Scene with groupKey 'how-to-evolving-scene' and a changing through payload.
Stage derives one group start and uses it as the grouped canvas key.
Scene supplies entity and stepCard IDs to Box, Arrow, SymbolChip, and Frame; those node implementations assign the IDs to layoutId.

subcomponents.title: Maintains clear boundaries and scope discipline

criteria.rationale: The required public title input is consumed: Talk supplies it to Presentation, which passes it to Header for the browse heading and to Footer for the live-title fallback. Step payloads drive the shared Scene, and the kit's canvas constants feed Stage and its fit calculation.
evidence: Talk supplies title; Presentation forwards it; Header renders title in browse mode.
Each step supplies through, which Scene reads to select the accumulated content.
Stage uses the default design dimensions and useFitScale reads STAGE_LAYOUT for the active mode.

criteria.rationale: Progress and section controls expose semantic current state and a stable active attribute that the demo's local CSS styles. Footer implements the default attribution in project source, and the demo's local CSS styles its link.
evidence: Footer progress buttons use aria-current and data-presentation-active; Toc section buttons use the same active hook.
Demo CSS targets the active hook for both controls and styles the attribution.
Footer's default is a locally rendered 'made by and-scene' GitHub link.

criteria.rationale: The registry points to the demo's Talk. Talk composes the shared Presentation boundary with presentation-local steps and CSS; the demo's scene state, entity IDs, content, and styles live in its own directory. The shared Presentation boundary contains generic hosting and chrome wiring rather than demo-specific branches.
evidence: The registry loads the demo Talk, which imports its local steps and style.
The local steps, Scene, entities, and CSS contain the demo implementation.
Presentation delegates generically to Header, Toc, Stage, and Footer using its props.

subcomponents.title: Step model, stable identity, and typed boundary

criteria.rationale: Each step has an ID, title, and caption. Presentation selects the active step, exposes its ID, and passes its narration to the footer.
evidence: StepMeta defines id, title, and caption; Presentation selects steps[nav.index] and renders Footer with that step.

criteria.rationale: Visible step numbers come from array indexes rather than authored number fields.
evidence: Footer renders index + 1 for the current step and itemIndex + 1 for progress buttons; the sample maps ordered beats to steps.

criteria.rationale: The generic payload type connects each step to its Scene, and Stage passes that payload through. A focused test renders two typed payload values across navigation.
evidence: Step<TPayload> pairs SceneProps<TPayload> with payload: TPayload; Stage invokes Scene with step.payload; the typed grouped-payload test asserts both values render.

subcomponents.title: Entity transitions and persistent grouped scenes

criteria.rationale: Stable entity IDs become Motion layout IDs inside a retained grouped scene and LayoutGroup, enabling layout changes to animate for continuing entities.
evidence: Stage keeps the grouped Scene mounted; Box assigns layoutId from its stable id and Stage wraps the scene in LayoutGroup.

criteria.rationale: Appear uses a fixed entry delay, while the continuing entities' layout motion does not consume the exported settlement configuration or signal completion to newcomers.
evidence: Appear defaults to ENTER_DELAY; Box supplies layoutId without LAYOUT_T; Stage provides no completion signal between continuing layout motion and Appear entry.

criteria.rationale: Ordinary authored conditional entities use Presence and exit props, and a focused integration test asserts that a removed Box remains during exit before disappearing.
evidence: The sample Scene wraps conditional entities in Presence; the departing-entity test checks immediate retention, retention after 80 ms, eventual removal, and survival of the continuing Box.

criteria.rationale: Adjacent steps with the same group key and Scene retain the canvas and Scene instance while receiving the new payload.
evidence: Stage keeps the grouped canvas keyed to groupStart and renders Scene with the current payload; the grouped-payload test asserts updated content with mountCount still one.

criteria.rationale: Grouped updates retain the Scene instance and stable keyed children. Appear's initial entry state therefore belongs to newly mounted entries, not continuing entries.
evidence: Stage preserves the grouped canvas key; the sample keeps existing card entries keyed by index inside Presence, and Appear defines its entry as an initial state.

criteria.rationale: The sample uses one grouped Scene whose payload drives persistent and accumulating entities across the ordered steps.
evidence: All sample steps share Scene and groupKey with an increasing through payload; Scene derives cardCount and conditionally adds entities from that payload.

subcomponents.title: Present/browse modes, navigation, controls, and boundaries

criteria.rationale: Present mode renders the active step title in the footer, omits browse progress and table of contents, and hides browse controls.
evidence: Footer switches to presentation-live-title in present mode; Presentation renders Toc only in browse mode; kit CSS hides present-mode controls.

criteria.rationale: Browse mode shows the active title and caption, a wide-viewport table of contents, previous and next controls, and progress buttons.
evidence: Footer renders caption, progress, and controls; Presentation renders Toc in browse mode; kit CSS hides Toc only below 760 px.

criteria.rationale: Mode and step index are separate state values, and toggling mode changes only mode. A focused test confirms the index remains unchanged.
evidence: toggleMode calls only setMode; the mode-switch test asserts present mode with data-step-index still 0.

criteria.rationale: The window key handler maps Right, Space, and PageDown to next; Left and PageUp to previous; and P to mode toggle.
evidence: usePresentationNav registers onKeyDown and calls next, prev, or toggleMode for those keys.

criteria.rationale: The handler rejects predominantly vertical movement but does not record or reject multi-touch gestures, and there are no focused vertical and multi-touch assertions.
evidence: onTouchStart takes touches[0] without checking touch count; onTouchEnd uses changedTouches[0]. The focused presentation tests contain no swipe rejection assertions.

criteria.rationale: Progress and table-of-contents buttons call goTo with their target indexes.
evidence: Footer maps each step to an onGoTo(itemIndex) button; Toc finds each era's first step and calls onGoTo(first).

criteria.rationale: The current progress step and current section expose semantic aria-current values and stable active data hooks.

criteria.rationale: goTo clamps negative targets to zero, and a focused test confirms Left on the first step stays at index zero.
evidence: goTo applies Math.max(0, ...); the boundary test sends ArrowLeft at index 0 and asserts index 0.

criteria.rationale: goTo clamps targets to the final index, and a focused test confirms repeated Right navigation stays on the last step.
evidence: goTo applies Math.min(count - 1, next); the boundary test sends ArrowRight twice in a two-step deck and asserts index 1.

subcomponents.title: Style ownership, hooks, framework neutrality, and attribution

criteria.rationale: The kit exposes stable classes and data attributes on its presentation chrome and scene primitives for host styling.
evidence: Presentation sets data-presentation and mode attributes; Box sets scene-box and data-presentation-node; Footer exposes caption, controls, progress, and attribution hooks.

criteria.rationale: Kit CSS supplies positioning and layout hooks without imposing colors, backgrounds, borders, or a presentation theme on scene primitives.
evidence: The kit stylesheet positions scene nodes; the primitive-style test asserts Box has no inline color, background, or border, while presentation-owned CSS supplies those visual treatments.

criteria.rationale: The delivered kit uses React components and ordinary CSS, with no styling-framework dependency required by the package.
evidence: The package dependencies contain React, Motion, and Lucide but no CSS framework; main imports the kit stylesheet directly, and the kit stylesheet uses standard CSS selectors.

criteria.rationale: Scene primitives accept positioning styles and the sample uses explicit coordinates for a diagram of persistent entities.
evidence: Box forwards its style to the motion element; kit CSS absolutely positions scene nodes; the sample Scene supplies left, top, width, and height for boxes and arrows.

criteria.rationale: The kit renders the default made by and-scene GitHub link and positions its container at the footer's bottom-right corner.
evidence: Footer supplies the default anchor; kit CSS positions .presentation-attribution with right and bottom offsets; the focused test asserts the link text and destination.

criteria.rationale: The default attribution has a stable class and data hook that host CSS can target.
evidence: Footer renders className='presentation-attribution' and data-presentation-attribution; presentation-owned CSS targets that class and its anchor.

criteria.rationale: The default top-left brand is empty, but the kit exposes no prop or content slot through which a host can supply branding; its empty brand element is hidden by kit CSS.
evidence: Header always renders an empty brand div; Presentation passes only title and mode to Header; .presentation-header-brand:empty sets display:none.

evidence: Section 1 covers topic, visual direction, and each step's content, then specifies one-at-a-time questioning.

criteria.rationale: The skill lets the user proceed with partial detail and directs the agent to fill gaps with minimal, labeled decisions without a completeness gate.
evidence: Section 1 explicitly permits proceeding after the user chooses partial detail.

criteria.rationale: The skill says to avoid asking for details already clear and to implement directly when the prompt is complete.
evidence: Section 1 states that a complete prompt can go directly to implementation.

The lockfile test uses npm ci --dry-run; it does not install dependencies.

criteria.rationale: The skill instructs reuse of existing anchors, but no focused executable test or verified workflow record constructs a target with all three anchors and verifies that scaffolding is skipped.
evidence: The bootstrap tests begin with empty temporary targets; neither sets up an already scaffolded target.

criteria.rationale: The instructions describe copying only missing contract pieces, but there is no focused executable evidence for a target with some anchors present, preservation of those anchors, and installation of missing dependencies.
evidence: The bootstrap tests copy a complete template into an empty target; they do not construct a partial scaffold.

criteria.rationale: The copied bootstrap app includes a starter presentation whose imported CSS supplies default colors, fonts, borders, shadows, and button treatments. The test checks the kit CSS for some style tokens but does not establish a style-neutral full scaffold.
evidence: Starter Talk imports style.css.
Starter style.css defines colored controls and a styled topic card.
The bootstrap test's neutrality assertion examines only presentation-kit.css.

criteria.rationale: The policy names skill-relative template paths, but the executable test resolves bootstrap from process.cwd() and does not exercise template lookup from the skill's own directory or dependency installation from a resolved target.
evidence: The test sets repo = process.cwd() and derives bootstrap with path.join(repo, 'skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap').

criteria.rationale: The policy selects presentations/ for a monorepo, but no focused executable test or verified workflow record constructs a monorepo and checks that the app is placed there while root files remain intact.
evidence: The bootstrap test uses an empty temporary target and contains no workspace or packages/apps setup.

criteria.rationale: The policy selects the root for standalone projects, but the test manually copies to a temporary root; it does not exercise standalone target detection or verify dependency installation in that selected root.
evidence: The bootstrap test assigns an empty temporary directory as target and calls cp directly, without a target-selection mechanism.

criteria.rationale: The instruction to wait for confirmation is explicit, but scaffold review requires focused executable or verified workflow evidence for an ambiguous nonempty target. None constructs that state and verifies the confirmation branch before mutation.
evidence: Both bootstrap test cases create empty temporary directories; neither models a user choice for a nonempty target.

AppRouter finds a matching slug and renders the lazily loaded presentation.

criteria.rationale: The skill assigns visual choices to presentation-owned CSS. The shared kit CSS supplies layout and positioning, while the sample presentation imports its own stylesheet containing its visual rules.
evidence: Section 3 assigns colors, fonts, spacing, borders, and treatments to presentation-owned CSS.
Talk imports its local style.css; the kit CSS contains positioning and layout rules.

criteria.rationale: The skill explicitly prohibits rewriting existing presentation files for a new presentation. The registry is an array of entries, and the router selects by slug, allowing an added route to coexist with existing entries.
evidence: Section 3 requires a new directory and says a new presentation must not rewrite existing presentation files.
The registry and AppRouter support distinct slug entries.

criteria.rationale: The skill explicitly requires listing registered presentations and asking which one to modify when the target is unspecified or ambiguous, before editing.
evidence: Section 1 directs target identification before modification and a choice request for ambiguous targets.

criteria.rationale: After target identification, the skill limits questions to requested edits and limits changes to the selected presentation plus the minimum necessary registry or shared-host files.
evidence: Sections 1 and 3 specify the modification interview and file scope.

evidence: Section 4 requires build and lint, a first-step render check, and inspection of first, last, and dense/key steps before reporting success.

criteria.rationale: The skill explicitly requires fixing functional failures and accidental visual collisions, rerunning build, render, and inspection, and withholding completion while any check fails.
evidence: Section 4 specifies the fix-and-repeat verification loop and the completion gate.

subcomponents.title: Verified candidate-produced testing evidence

criteria.rationale: The candidate exercised substantial runtime and verification behavior, but did not exercise the presentation skill’s interactive creation, scaffolding, modification, or repair journeys. Together these omissions leave a substantial share of the added user-visible behavior untested, although they were disclosed.
evidence: The exploration log records browser navigation, mode switching, scene transitions, responsive scaling, build and render checks, and inspection diagnostics.
The exploration log explicitly says no independent skill-agent invocation was available for the authoring journeys or repair loop.

criteria.rationale: The claimed exercised behaviors have verified records describing concrete actions and observed results. The record identifies the narrow-view failure and measured exit behavior; it does not rely on defective screenshots for those conclusions.
evidence: The exploration log records step changes, input methods, active-state attributes, mode behavior, verifier output, and inspection results.
The findings history records the 390×168.4 px narrow canvas, approximately 5.8 px rendered labels, and measured departure delays of about 307–317 ms.
Verified screenshot descriptions and verified narrow and transition screenshots support the recorded visual observations.

criteria.rationale: The last recorded tested revision is the final revision. The candidate also records that the last pass found no changes from its prior tested revision, consistent with the harness-computed zero-file diff.
evidence: The verified tested-revision artifact records ac4ff930b9eb58173fabc783c56a470cded91041.
The verified index identifies that SHA as final and lists zero product, test-only, and harness changes to final.
The round-2 exploration log records reproduction of both prior findings at that SHA.

criteria.rationale: The candidate reports a NOT READY outcome, keeps the narrow-legibility finding open, distinguishes the resolved exit finding, and discloses the unexercised skill journeys, later-round test limits, simulated touch input, and absent automated CI checks.
evidence: The final handoff says acceptance did not converge; the round-2 handoff reports F-1 open and F-2 resolved.
The exploration log lists the skill-agent and repair-loop limitations, synthetic touch input, checks not repeated in later rounds, and the lack of automated build/test CI status.
The assumptions ledger discusses the remaining design decisions and the unresolved narrow-view finding.

subcomponents.title: Observable assumption handling

criteria.rationale: The candidate recorded consequential gaps and their effects, including unresolved narrow-screen readability, starter-route handling, and the active-navigation diagnostic.
evidence: The assumptions ledger lists U3, U4, and U5 with evidence and decision options.
The findings history keeps F-1 open after reproducing unreadable labels at the final tested revision.

criteria.rationale: The candidate reproduced a false active-navigation warning for a visibly distinct border state, then classified it as an unresolved policy choice rather than a finding against the approved diagnostic behavior.
evidence: The exploration log says a red border was the active state's sole distinction and the inspector still warned that it may look inactive.
INT-002 calls for warnings on indistinct active chrome; the skill directs review of indistinct active-navigation warnings.
The assumptions ledger labels this reproduced behavior U4 and says it is “not classified as a defect.”

criteria.rationale: Treating the reproduced false warning as optional diagnostic policy leaves nonconforming behavior without a finding or required correction. The proposed acceptance of unreadable phone labels would also require an explicit change to the approved readability requirement.
evidence: U4 offers “Leave as-is” despite the reproduced border-only false warning.
U5 recommends accepting narrow portrait as best-effort and amending the test-plan wording, while AT-003 requires important content to remain readable at narrow widths.

criteria.rationale: The final handoff states only that acceptance did not converge and links to other files. It omits the open readability decision, its options and consequences, other unresolved assumptions, and the agent-workflow testing limitation.
evidence: The final handoff contains a NOT_READY reason and paths to findings, assumptions, and tester handoff, but no decision summary.
The assumptions ledger contains unresolved U1, U3, U4, and U5; the exploration log records that required skill-agent journeys could not be exercised.

demo-integration.rationale: Talk passes its steps to the kit's Presentation component. The shared Scene uses exported kit primitives for its diagram, while Presentation and Stage provide navigation and scene hosting.
evidence: Talk renders <Presentation steps={STEPS}>.
Scene renders SceneLayer, Box, Arrow, Label, Presence, and other kit exports; Stage renders the active Scene from each step.

demo-integration.rationale: The nine entries generated from beats use the same Scene and groupKey. Stage keeps one keyed canvas mounted across those adjacent steps. Separately, Scene passes presentation-owned entity IDs to kit nodes that use them as motion layoutId values; step cards receive stable IDs from stepCard(index).
evidence: STEPS maps every beat to Scene with groupKey 'how-to-evolving-scene' and a changing through payload.
Stage derives one group start and uses it as the grouped canvas key.
Scene supplies entity and stepCard IDs to Box, Arrow, SymbolChip, and Frame; those node implementations assign the IDs to layoutId.

demo-integration.rationale: The required public title input is consumed: Talk supplies it to Presentation, which passes it to Header for the browse heading and to Footer for the live-title fallback. Step payloads drive the shared Scene, and the kit's canvas constants feed Stage and its fit calculation.
evidence: Talk supplies title; Presentation forwards it; Header renders title in browse mode.
Each step supplies through, which Scene reads to select the accumulated content.
Stage uses the default design dimensions and useFitScale reads STAGE_LAYOUT for the active mode.

demo-integration.rationale: Progress and section controls expose semantic current state and a stable active attribute that the demo's local CSS styles. Footer implements the default attribution in project source, and the demo's local CSS styles its link.
evidence: Footer progress buttons use aria-current and data-presentation-active; Toc section buttons use the same active hook.
Demo CSS targets the active hook for both controls and styles the attribution.
Footer's default is a locally rendered 'made by and-scene' GitHub link.

demo-integration.rationale: The registry points to the demo's Talk. Talk composes the shared Presentation boundary with presentation-local steps and CSS; the demo's scene state, entity IDs, content, and styles live in its own directory. The shared Presentation boundary contains generic hosting and chrome wiring rather than demo-specific branches.
evidence: The registry loads the demo Talk, which imports its local steps and style.
The local steps, Scene, entities, and CSS contain the demo implementation.
Presentation delegates generically to Header, Toc, Stage, and Footer using its props.

scene-kit.rationale: Each step has an ID, title, and caption. Presentation selects the active step, exposes its ID, and passes its narration to the footer.
evidence: StepMeta defines id, title, and caption; Presentation selects steps[nav.index] and renders Footer with that step.

scene-kit.rationale: Visible step numbers come from array indexes rather than authored number fields.
evidence: Footer renders index + 1 for the current step and itemIndex + 1 for progress buttons; the sample maps ordered beats to steps.

scene-kit.rationale: The generic payload type connects each step to its Scene, and Stage passes that payload through. A focused test renders two typed payload values across navigation.
evidence: Step<TPayload> pairs SceneProps<TPayload> with payload: TPayload; Stage invokes Scene with step.payload; the typed grouped-payload test asserts both values render.

scene-kit.rationale: Stable entity IDs become Motion layout IDs inside a retained grouped scene and LayoutGroup, enabling layout changes to animate for continuing entities.
evidence: Stage keeps the grouped Scene mounted; Box assigns layoutId from its stable id and Stage wraps the scene in LayoutGroup.

scene-kit.rationale: Appear uses a fixed entry delay, while the continuing entities' layout motion does not consume the exported settlement configuration or signal completion to newcomers.
evidence: Appear defaults to ENTER_DELAY; Box supplies layoutId without LAYOUT_T; Stage provides no completion signal between continuing layout motion and Appear entry.

scene-kit.rationale: Ordinary authored conditional entities use Presence and exit props, and a focused integration test asserts that a removed Box remains during exit before disappearing.
evidence: The sample Scene wraps conditional entities in Presence; the departing-entity test checks immediate retention, retention after 80 ms, eventual removal, and survival of the continuing Box.

scene-kit.rationale: Adjacent steps with the same group key and Scene retain the canvas and Scene instance while receiving the new payload.
evidence: Stage keeps the grouped canvas keyed to groupStart and renders Scene with the current payload; the grouped-payload test asserts updated content with mountCount still one.

scene-kit.rationale: Grouped updates retain the Scene instance and stable keyed children. Appear's initial entry state therefore belongs to newly mounted entries, not continuing entries.
evidence: Stage preserves the grouped canvas key; the sample keeps existing card entries keyed by index inside Presence, and Appear defines its entry as an initial state.

scene-kit.rationale: The sample uses one grouped Scene whose payload drives persistent and accumulating entities across the ordered steps.
evidence: All sample steps share Scene and groupKey with an increasing through payload; Scene derives cardCount and conditionally adds entities from that payload.

scene-kit.rationale: Present mode renders the active step title in the footer, omits browse progress and table of contents, and hides browse controls.
evidence: Footer switches to presentation-live-title in present mode; Presentation renders Toc only in browse mode; kit CSS hides present-mode controls.

scene-kit.rationale: Browse mode shows the active title and caption, a wide-viewport table of contents, previous and next controls, and progress buttons.
evidence: Footer renders caption, progress, and controls; Presentation renders Toc in browse mode; kit CSS hides Toc only below 760 px.

scene-kit.rationale: Mode and step index are separate state values, and toggling mode changes only mode. A focused test confirms the index remains unchanged.
evidence: toggleMode calls only setMode; the mode-switch test asserts present mode with data-step-index still 0.

scene-kit.rationale: The window key handler maps Right, Space, and PageDown to next; Left and PageUp to previous; and P to mode toggle.
evidence: usePresentationNav registers onKeyDown and calls next, prev, or toggleMode for those keys.

scene-kit.rationale: The handler rejects predominantly vertical movement but does not record or reject multi-touch gestures, and there are no focused vertical and multi-touch assertions.
evidence: onTouchStart takes touches[0] without checking touch count; onTouchEnd uses changedTouches[0]. The focused presentation tests contain no swipe rejection assertions.

scene-kit.rationale: Progress and table-of-contents buttons call goTo with their target indexes.
evidence: Footer maps each step to an onGoTo(itemIndex) button; Toc finds each era's first step and calls onGoTo(first).

scene-kit.rationale: The current progress step and current section expose semantic aria-current values and stable active data hooks.
evidence: Footer sets aria-current='step' and data-presentation-active from index equality; Toc sets aria-current='location' and the active hook from era equality; a focused test asserts both c…

scene-kit.rationale: Presentation navigation returns early for focused interactive controls, preserving their keyboard behavior.
evidence: onKeyDown excludes INPUT, TEXTAREA, SELECT, BUTTON, A, and editable targets; the focused-button test sends ArrowRight to Next and asserts the step does not change.

scene-kit.rationale: goTo clamps negative targets to zero, and a focused test confirms Left on the first step stays at index zero.
evidence: goTo applies Math.max(0, ...); the boundary test sends ArrowLeft at index 0 and asserts index 0.

scene-kit.rationale: goTo clamps targets to the final index, and a focused test confirms repeated Right navigation stays on the last step.
evidence: goTo applies Math.min(count - 1, next); the boundary test sends ArrowRight twice in a two-step deck and asserts index 1.

scene-kit.rationale: The canvas uses one scale factor, but the stage centers it in the entire viewport after fit calculations reserve unequal top and bottom chrome space. At an ordinary 900×600 viewport, the computed browse canvas extends below the reserved available area.
evidence: useFitScale reserves 82 px above and 164 px below in browse mode, giving a 354 px available height; Stage scales the canvas to that height, while .presentation-stage centers it in the full 600 px vie…

scene-kit.rationale: The rendered Stage defaults to the approved 880×380 authored canvas.
evidence: DESIGN_W and DESIGN_H are 880 and 380; Stage uses them as default props and applies designWidth and designHeight to the canvas.

scene-kit.rationale: The kit exposes stable classes and data attributes on its presentation chrome and scene primitives for host styling.
evidence: Presentation sets data-presentation and mode attributes; Box sets scene-box and data-presentation-node; Footer exposes caption, controls, progress, and attribution hooks.

scene-kit.rationale: Kit CSS supplies positioning and layout hooks without imposing colors, backgrounds, borders, or a presentation theme on scene primitives.
evidence: The kit stylesheet positions scene nodes; the primitive-style test asserts Box has no inline color, background, or border, while presentation-owned CSS supplies those visual treatments.

scene-kit.rationale: The delivered kit uses React components and ordinary CSS, with no styling-framework dependency required by the package.
evidence: The package dependencies contain React, Motion, and Lucide but no CSS framework; main imports the kit stylesheet directly, and the kit stylesheet uses standard CSS selectors.

scene-kit.rationale: Scene primitives accept positioning styles and the sample uses explicit coordinates for a diagram of persistent entities.
evidence: Box forwards its style to the motion element; kit CSS absolutely positions scene nodes; the sample Scene supplies left, top, width, and height for boxes and arrows.

scene-kit.rationale: The kit renders the default made by and-scene GitHub link and positions its container at the footer's bottom-right corner.
evidence: Footer supplies the default anchor; kit CSS positions .presentation-attribution with right and bottom offsets; the focused test asserts the link text and destination.

scene-kit.rationale: The default attribution has a stable class and data hook that host CSS can target.
evidence: Footer renders className='presentation-attribution' and data-presentation-attribution; presentation-owned CSS targets that class and its anchor.

scene-kit.rationale: The default top-left brand is empty, but the kit exposes no prop or content slot through which a host can supply branding; its empty brand element is hidden by kit CSS.
evidence: Header always renders an empty brand div; Presentation passes only title and mode to Header; .presentation-header-brand:empty sets display:none.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill explicitly requires one concise question at a time and directs the agent to ask for the next missing detail after checking the prompt and supplied files.
evidence: Section 1 covers topic, visual direction, and each step's content, then specifies one-at-a-time questioning.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill lets the user proceed with partial detail and directs the agent to fill gaps with minimal, labeled decisions without a completeness gate.
evidence: Section 1 explicitly permits proceeding after the user chooses partial detail.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill says to avoid asking for details already clear and to implement directly when the prompt is complete.
evidence: Section 1 states that a complete prompt can go directly to implementation.

presentation-skill.rationale: The empty-directory test copies and builds the bootstrap template, but it links an existing node_modules directory and never verifies installation of dependencies into the resolved target. It therefore does not prove the full scaffold outcome required for this branch.
evidence: The 'materializes, builds from an unrelated working directory' test creates an empty temporary target, copies the template, and symlinks the repository's node_modules.
The lockfile test uses npm ci --dry-run; it does not install dependencies.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill instructs reuse of existing anchors, but no focused executable test or verified workflow record constructs a target with all three anchors and verifies that scaffolding is skipped.
evidence: The bootstrap tests begin with empty temporary targets; neither sets up an already scaffolded target.

presentation-skill.rationale: The instructions describe copying only missing contract pieces, but there is no focused executable evidence for a target with some anchors present, preservation of those anchors, and installation of missing dependencies.
evidence: The bootstrap tests copy a complete template into an empty target; they do not construct a partial scaffold.

presentation-skill.rationale: The copied bootstrap app includes a starter presentation whose imported CSS supplies default colors, fonts, borders, shadows, and button treatments. The test checks the kit CSS for some style tokens but does not establish a style-neutral full scaffold.
evidence: Starter Talk imports style.css.
Starter style.css defines colored controls and a styled topic card.
The bootstrap test's neutrality assertion examines only presentation-kit.css.

presentation-skill.rationale: The policy names skill-relative template paths, but the executable test resolves bootstrap from process.cwd() and does not exercise template lookup from the skill's own directory or dependency installation from a resolved target.
evidence: The test sets repo = process.cwd() and derives bootstrap with path.join(repo, 'skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap').

presentation-skill.rationale: The policy selects presentations/ for a monorepo, but no focused executable test or verified workflow record constructs a monorepo and checks that the app is placed there while root files remain intact.
evidence: The bootstrap test uses an empty temporary target and contains no workspace or packages/apps setup.

presentation-skill.rationale: The policy selects the root for standalone projects, but the test manually copies to a temporary root; it does not exercise standalone target detection or verify dependency installation in that selected root.
evidence: The bootstrap test assigns an empty temporary directory as target and calls cp directly, without a target-selection mechanism.

presentation-skill.rationale: The instruction to wait for confirmation is explicit, but scaffold review requires focused executable or verified workflow evidence for an ambiguous nonempty target. None constructs that state and verifies the confirmation branch before mutation.
evidence: Both bootstrap test cases create empty temporary directories; neither models a user choice for a nonempty target.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill requires a presentation-specific directory and one lazy registry entry. The registry stores slug, title, and loader, and AppRouter resolves the current pathname to that loader.
evidence: Section 3 directs creation under src/presentations/<slug>/ and registration.
AppRouter finds a matching slug and renders the lazily loaded presentation.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill assigns visual choices to presentation-owned CSS. The shared kit CSS supplies layout and positioning, while the sample presentation imports its own stylesheet containing its visual rules.
evidence: Section 3 assigns colors, fonts, spacing, borders, and treatments to presentation-owned CSS.
Talk imports its local style.css; the kit CSS contains positioning and layout rules.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill explicitly prohibits rewriting existing presentation files for a new presentation. The registry is an array of entries, and the router selects by slug, allowing an added route to coexist with existing entries.
evidence: Section 3 requires a new directory and says a new presentation must not rewrite existing presentation files.
The registry and AppRouter support distinct slug entries.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill explicitly requires listing registered presentations and asking which one to modify when the target is unspecified or ambiguous, before editing.
evidence: Section 1 directs target identification before modification and a choice request for ambiguous targets.

presentation-skill.rationale: After target identification, the skill limits questions to requested edits and limits changes to the selected presentation plus the minimum necessary registry or shared-host files.
evidence: Sections 1 and 3 specify the modification interview and file scope.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill explicitly gates success on build, lint, route render without console or runtime errors, and browser screenshot inspection of representative steps.
evidence: Section 4 requires build and lint, a first-step render check, and inspection of first, last, and dense/key steps before reporting success.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill explicitly requires fixing functional failures and accidental visual collisions, rerunning build, render, and inspection, and withholding completion while any check fails.
evidence: Section 4 specifies the fix-and-repeat verification loop and the completion gate.

verification-tooling.rationale: The verifier rejects an absent canonical registry entry and sets a nonzero exit code.
evidence: The missing-slug branch throws before preview startup; the top-level catch sets process.exitCode to 1.
The isolated-copy test removes the registry entry and asserts the missing-sample failure message.

verification-tooling.rationale: Preview binding and browser URLs consistently use the returned 127.0.0.1 address.
evidence: startPreview binds to 127.0.0.1 and returns that host with its assigned port; both verifier and screenshot helper build their URLs from those values.

verification-tooling.rationale: The cited implementation starts Vite preview in the verifier's process. It does not start or monitor a preview child process, as the criterion requires.
evidence: source audit: scripts/preview-utils.mjs imports preview from vite and calls await preview(...) directly; it contains no child-process spawn or exit check.
source audit: scripts/verify.mjs calls startPreview() and navigates to its returned port.

verification-tooling.rationale: Console and page errors are collected by the verifier, but the focused regression exercises only a console error. There is no focused executable evidence that a page error propagates with its failing step.
evidence: The test case 'identifies browser console and non-advancing transition faults by step' injects console.error and a blocked key transition; it does not inject a pageerror.

verification-tooling.rationale: A stalled step transition produces a nonzero verification result that identifies the failing step.
evidence: The verifier wraps step navigation failures with the current step number. The isolated-copy transition test blocks ArrowRight, then asserts nonzero status, 'step 1', and timeout or transition…

verification-tooling.rationale: The project provides an implemented screenshot inspection command that the presentation skill invokes.
evidence: The inspect script starts preview, opens the presentation in Playwright, and writes step screenshots; package.json exposes it as npm run inspect, which the skill directs users to run.

verification-tooling.rationale: The helper captures each reported step from the preview address it started, and an executable template test exercises a two-step capture.
evidence: The helper navigates using startPreview’s returned host and port, loops over data-step-count, waits for each step index, and screenshots before advancing. The bootstrap test creates two steps, runs i…

verification-tooling.rationale: Capture uses a fixed timeout rather than observing animation completion or consuming a transition contract used by runtime motion.
evidence: The helper waits PRESENTATION_SETTLE_MS or 1100 ms before each screenshot. Runtime Appear motion consumes ENTER_DELAY and ENTER_T, but the helper neither observes that motion nor imports its transiti…

verification-tooling.rationale: The diagnostic measures rendered text and control rectangles and emits a warning for intersecting, unrelated elements; a browser fixture asserts an overlap warning.
evidence: inspectDiagnostics compares visible presentation text and chrome rectangles. The focused browser test places a paragraph across the navigation controls and asserts a 'possible visible text/chrome…

verification-tooling.rationale: Marked intentional overlap is suppressed while the browser fixture still asserts an unrelated collision warning.
evidence: inspectDiagnostics skips pairs containing an element beneath data-allow-overlap. The focused fixture overlaps a marked paragraph with another paragraph, asserts no warning names 'intentional'…

verification-tooling.rationale: The diagnostic compares computed styles of rendered active and inactive controls, and a browser fixture asserts the warning when those styles match.
evidence: inspectDiagnostics compares color, backgroundColor, and fontWeight across data-presentation-active states. The focused test gives active and inactive buttons identical styles and asserts the active-n…

verification-tooling.rationale: The implementation includes missing, default-style, and small-text checks, but focused executable evidence covers missing and default attribution only. The required undersized-attribution warning is not exercised.
evidence: The browser tests assert warnings for absent attribution and a default-styled link. Neither fixture sets an undersized font and asserts its warning.

testing-evidence.rationale: The candidate exercised substantial runtime and verification behavior, but did not exercise the presentation skill’s interactive creation, scaffolding, modification, or repair journeys. Together these omissions leave a substantial share of the added user-visible behavior untested, although they were disclosed.
evidence: The exploration log records browser navigation, mode switching, scene transitions, responsive scaling, build and render checks, and inspection diagnostics.
The exploration log explicitly says no independent skill-agent invocation was available for the authoring journeys or repair loop.

testing-evidence.rationale: The claimed exercised behaviors have verified records describing concrete actions and observed results. The record identifies the narrow-view failure and measured exit behavior; it does not rely on defective screenshots for those conclusions.
evidence: The exploration log records step changes, input methods, active-state attributes, mode behavior, verifier output, and inspection results.
The findings history records the 390×168.4 px narrow canvas, approximately 5.8 px rendered labels, and measured departure delays of about 307–317 ms.
Verified screenshot descriptions and verified narrow and transition screenshots support the recorded visual observations.

testing-evidence.rationale: The last recorded tested revision is the final revision. The candidate also records that the last pass found no changes from its prior tested revision, consistent with the harness-computed zero-file diff.
evidence: The verified tested-revision artifact records ac4ff930b9eb58173fabc783c56a470cded91041.
The verified index identifies that SHA as final and lists zero product, test-only, and harness changes to final.
The round-2 exploration log records reproduction of both prior findings at that SHA.

testing-evidence.rationale: The candidate reports a NOT READY outcome, keeps the narrow-legibility finding open, distinguishes the resolved exit finding, and discloses the unexercised skill journeys, later-round test limits, simulated touch input, and absent automated CI checks.
evidence: The final handoff says acceptance did not converge; the round-2 handoff reports F-1 open and F-2 resolved.
The exploration log lists the skill-agent and repair-loop limitations, synthetic touch input, checks not repeated in later rounds, and the lack of automated build/test CI status.
The assumptions ledger discusses the remaining design decisions and the unresolved narrow-view finding.

assumption-handling.rationale: The candidate recorded consequential gaps and their effects, including unresolved narrow-screen readability, starter-route handling, and the active-navigation diagnostic.
evidence: The assumptions ledger lists U3, U4, and U5 with evidence and decision options.
The findings history keeps F-1 open after reproducing unreadable labels at the final tested revision.

assumption-handling.rationale: The candidate reproduced a false active-navigation warning for a visibly distinct border state, then classified it as an unresolved policy choice rather than a finding against the approved diagnostic behavior.
evidence: The exploration log says a red border was the active state's sole distinction and the inspector still warned that it may look inactive.
INT-002 calls for warnings on indistinct active chrome; the skill directs review of indistinct active-navigation warnings.
The assumptions ledger labels this reproduced behavior U4 and says it is “not classified as a defect.”

assumption-handling.rationale: Treating the reproduced false warning as optional diagnostic policy leaves nonconforming behavior without a finding or required correction. The proposed acceptance of unreadable phone labels would also require an explicit change to the approved readability requirement.
evidence: U4 offers “Leave as-is” despite the reproduced border-only false warning.
U5 recommends accepting narrow portrait as best-effort and amending the test-plan wording, while AT-003 requires important content to remain readable at narrow widths.

assumption-handling.rationale: The final handoff states only that acceptance did not converge and links to other files. It omits the open readability decision, its options and consequences, other unresolved assumptions, and the agent-workflow testing limitation.
evidence: The final handoff contains a NOT_READY reason and paths to findings, assumptions, and tester handoff, but no decision summary.
The assumptions ledger contains unresolved U1, U3, U4, and U5; the exploration log records that required skill-agent journeys could not be exercised.

evidence: Talk.tsx renders Presentation with STEPS.
steps/Scene.tsx imports and renders exported primitives including SceneLayer, Box, Arrow, Label, and Presence; presentation-kit/index.ts exports them.
Presentation.tsx passes the steps to Stage.tsx, which renders the active step's Scene.

evidence: steps/index.ts maps every one of the nine beats to Scene with groupKey 'how-to-evolving-scene' and payload.through set to its index.
Stage.tsx finds the start of adjacent steps with matching groupKey and Scene, then keys the grouped canvas by that start.

Box.tsx, Arrow.tsx, SymbolChip.tsx, and Frame.tsx assign the supplied IDs to motion layoutId.

Presentation.tsx uses generic steps, title, dimensions, mode, and attribution props to wire Header, Toc, Stage, and Footer.

evidence: types.ts defines StepMeta with id, title, and caption.
Presentation.tsx selects steps[nav.index], exposes step.id, and passes step to Footer.tsx.

scene-kit.rationale: The visible current number and progress numbers come from step indexes.
evidence: Footer.tsx renders index + 1 and itemIndex + 1.
steps/index.ts creates the sample steps in beat order.

scene-kit.rationale: The generic step type connects the scene and payload types, and the stage passes the payload through. A focused test covers updates.
evidence: types.ts pairs SceneProps<TPayload> with payload: TPayload in Step<TPayload>.
Stage.tsx renders Scene with step.payload; Presentation.test.tsx asserts both typed payload values across navigation.

scene-kit.rationale: Stable entity identity is connected to an implemented layout animation path in a retained grouped scene.
evidence: Box.tsx sets motion.div layoutId to layoutId ?? id.
Stage.tsx retains the grouped canvas and Scene instance and wraps them in LayoutGroup.

evidence: Appear.tsx defaults to ENTER_DELAY and uses it in its entry transition.
Box.tsx sets layoutId but no layout transition using LAYOUT_T; Stage.tsx supplies no completion signal.

scene-kit.rationale: Authored conditional entities use Presence, and a focused integration test checks retention during exit and eventual removal.

Presentation.test.tsx checks that a removed Box remains immediately and after 80 ms, later disappears, and leaves the continuing Box mounted.

scene-kit.rationale: Adjacent steps sharing a group and Scene retain the Scene instance while receiving updated payload.
evidence: Stage.tsx keys the grouped canvas by groupStart and renders Scene with the current step.payload.
Presentation.test.tsx asserts updated content while mountCount remains one.

scene-kit.rationale: The grouped Scene stays mounted, and continuing keyed children stay on the same render path; Appear's initial state applies to newly mounted children.
evidence: Stage.tsx retains the grouped canvas across adjacent updates.
Scene.tsx renders continuing cards with stable index keys inside Presence; Appear.tsx defines entry with initial and animate states.

scene-kit.rationale: The sample deliberately uses one grouped Scene whose payload grows the composition over ordered steps.
evidence: steps/index.ts assigns every step the same Scene and groupKey with an increasing through payload.
Scene.tsx derives cardCount and conditional entities from through; Stage.tsx retains the grouped Scene.

scene-kit.rationale: Present mode shows the active title and removes browse navigation chrome.
evidence: Footer.tsx renders presentation-live-title in present mode and renders progress only in browse mode.
Presentation.tsx renders Toc only in browse mode; presentation-kit.css hides present-mode controls.

scene-kit.rationale: Browse mode supplies the active title and caption, table of contents at wide widths, controls, and progress.
evidence: Footer.tsx renders the active title, caption, previous and next buttons, and progress buttons.
Presentation.tsx renders Toc in browse mode; presentation-kit.css hides it only below 760px.

scene-kit.rationale: Mode toggling leaves the step index unchanged, as a focused test verifies.
evidence: usePresentationNav.ts toggleMode updates only mode.
Presentation.test.tsx asserts present mode while data-step-index remains 0.

scene-kit.rationale: The window keyboard handler implements the claimed navigation and mode keys.

The script then throws 'departing reveal frame was removed immediately' even though the exit animation worked. The inverse is also possible: on a slow machine the element may never be observed mid-exit, so the check proves nothing. Either way `npm run verify` can fail intermittently.
